items.title: Bob Kinkel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 31, 2012
items.q: So like Steve Gadd would be there, you know, “yeah, how you doing.” “Good.” “Okay, see you, I’ve got to go do some dog food thing in ten minutes.”

ctx.x: What about hiring other session players? Was that a part of what you did? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -10-

A little bit. Not as much. If it was something I was doing with Charlie or something I was more involved in production on, yeah, you need a guitar part you’d call in like Elliot Randall or someone to come in. It was fun. I did like a lot of just showing up as a keyboard player to sessions too, and you never knew if you’d be on the session. So like Steve Gadd would be there, you know, “yeah, how you doing.” “Good.” “Okay, see you, I’ve got to go do some dog food thing in ten minutes.” And so there was a lot of the…
As a session player, you rarely knew what you were going to be called on to play, music- wise, is that correct?
